newsitem.title: JAPAN: Toshiba launches line-up of tiny electronic goods.
newsitem.headline: Toshiba launches line-up of tiny electronic goods.

text.p: Japanese electronics giant Toshiba Corp on Monday unveiled its latest in a series of new miniaturised electronic gadgets: a business card-sized digital camera.
The Allegretto, which it says is the world's smallest and lightest digital camera, joins a line-up of tiny Toshiba devices ranging from the Genio communicator to the Libretto notebook computer.
Toshiba has launched a number of high-technology gadgets since the beginning of the year, driven by technology advances and business people's demands for faster and more mobile communications.
"We are eyeing the tendency towards mobile computing, or the ability to send and receive information through multimedia systems from outdoors," a Toshiba spokesman said.
"The advances in semiconductor technology also make it possible to develop smaller and better products," he added.

The company's new mini-digital still camera, to debut in Japan and the United States this summer, weighs 130 grams and is the first to use a one-quarter inch 330,000-pixel complementary metal oxide semiconductor (CMOS) image sensor, which uses one-tenth the power of conventional models, the company said.
Earlier this month, Toshiba introduced the latest version of its Libretto miniature notebook personal computer (PC), the Libretto 50CT.
Introduced in Japan in April 1996, the Libretto is the world's smallest, lightest Windows 95-based PC, Toshiba said.

Toshiba also earlier this year unveiled the Genio, the world's smallest and lightest Internet viewer, which combines the functions of electronic mail, Internet access and the PHS wireless phone system.
